The image shows a pulled soybean plant held in hand with:
- Roots exposed and pulled from soil
- Stem appears bleached/white to pale yellow-white in color
- Leaves are collapsed, wilted, and appear dark gray-green to brown/necrotic
- The stem is bleached and appears soft/watery in texture
- No obvious black sclerotia visible at this resolution, but the bleached white stem is very characteristic

Key observations:
- Bleached white stem coloration
- Wilted, collapsed leaves that are still attached
- Plant appears to have died and been pulled from soil
- The stem has a characteristic blanched/white appearance typical of White Mold

White Mold matches strongly: "infected stems become soft, watery, and bleached white," "leaves turn gray-green then brown and remain attached," and the overall collapsed plant appearance. The white/pale bleached stem is the most distinctive feature here.
